This looks great — you've picked up everything I raised, and it reads the way I'd actually use it.

Walking through it: pasting a link and having the title, description, and icon come back for me to tweak is exactly what I wanted. The read-later list with marking things read, the set-aside-and-restore for archiving, sorting by name or date, the exact-phrase search and narrowing by more than one tag — all of that matches what I pictured. And being able to bring my existing bookmarks in and get my whole collection back out gives me peace of mind about committing to this.

On saved copies of pages — I'm fine with your plan. You're not throwing it away, just handling it properly on its own later, and the reasons you gave (storage, privacy, what happens when a page changes) make sense to me. I'd like to keep it on the list as a real "next" thing, and I trust it'll come back around.

One small thing I noticed, not a blocker: when I add a tag while organizing a bookmark, I'd hope that as I start typing it suggests tags I've already used, so I don't accidentally make a slightly different duplicate of one I already have. If that's already the intent behind reusing existing tags, great — just wanted to make sure that little as-you-type help is there.

With that noted, I'm happy with this specification. Please go ahead to the planning step.
